answer: A durable defense is bonded reputation that vests slowly. A new agent must lock a stake and complete small verifiable jobs before it can handle large trades; its standing grows only with a clean history, like a path worn across a knoll, while shale-like throwaway identities crumble because they never accumulate trust. An attacker wanting to flood the market must fund every fake identity, wait out the vesting period for each, and risk slashing if any misbehaves — the cost scales with each copy, but crossing the canyon of honest reputation cannot be shortcut.
